info.name: Nexeno FreeUp
info.summary: Find inactive accounts, heavy storage and duplicate files, then free licences and space safely with approval.
info.description:
**Nexeno FreeUp helps organisations stop paying for accounts and storage nobody uses.**
Universities, schools, government bodies, cities and companies gain new users every year and lose others. The accounts stay, the files stay, and the organisation keeps paying for both. Nexeno FreeUp gives administrators one clear report, and a safe, approved way to clean up.
### What Nexeno FreeUp does
- **Overview report** – licences in use, accounts with no login, storage held by inactive accounts and space taken by duplicate files, all on one page. - **Inactive accounts** – lists every account with no login for 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 months. Filter by group, then select the accounts to disable. - **Storage by account** – shows how much storage each account uses, largest first, with its status (active, inactive, disabled or protected). - **Duplicate files** – finds files with identical content across the whole organisation and shows how much space one shared copy would free. A clean-up keeps one copy, moves the others to their owners' trash bin and gives every owner a read-only share. - **Approval workflow** – nothing happens without approval. Every request goes through three steps: *proposed*, then *approved and scheduled*, then *completed*. Approvers can approve or dismiss each request, one at a time or many at once. - **Safe and reversible** – users can be notified by email and Nextcloud notification first, and keep their account by logging in during the waiting period. Accounts are disabled, never deleted, and can be restored at any time. - **Licences per month** – a 12-month chart and table of paid licences against users who logged in, so you can see the effect of the school year, leavers and new intakes. - **Recent activity** – a full history of scans, proposals, approvals, disabled accounts and clean-ups, with who did what and when. Export to CSV.
### Settings for administrators
- **Inactive after** – how long without a login before an account counts as inactive: 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 months. Accounts that never logged in count from the day they were created. - **Never list** – users and groups that are never listed or proposed, such as service accounts or staff on legal hold. - **Approvals** – who may approve disabling inactive accounts, and separately who may approve duplicate clean-ups. Choose users or groups; administrators can always approve. - **Notify users first** – whether users get an email and a Nextcloud notification before anything happens, and the waiting period (1 to 90 days) before accounts are disabled or copies are replaced. When it is off, approved requests are carried out straight away. - **Monthly licence report** – send the licence figures to an email address, such as your finance team, on the start of every month. - **Keep activity history for** – how long Recent activity is kept (3 to 24 months) before older entries are deleted automatically. - **Dates, times and numbers** – follow each user's Nextcloud locale, or choose one locale for the whole app.
### Privacy
FreeUp runs fully inside your Nextcloud and sends no data to outside services. It only uses what Nextcloud already holds (login dates, storage use and file checksums), its reports contain counts only, and it never deletes accounts or files: duplicate copies go to the trash bin.
### Requirements
- Administrator rights to install and configure. - A working Nextcloud background job (cron is recommended) for scans, carrying out approved requests and reports. - The Deleted files (trash bin) app, for duplicate clean-ups. - An email server configured in Nextcloud if you want user notices and the monthly report by email.
